artists.biography: Jellyfish were a power pop band from San Francisco. It formed after Beatnik Beatch broke up in 1989. The core members were drummer, singer and songwriter Andy Sturmer and keyboardist, multi-instrumentalist, singer and songwriter Roger Joseph Manning, Jr. Although their career was short, the band has become highly influential in the power pop genre.

Jellyfish.biography: Jellyfish were a power pop band from San Francisco. It formed after Beatnik Beatch broke up in 1989. The core members were drummer, singer and songwriter Andy Sturmer and keyboardist, multi-instrumentalist, singer and songwriter Roger Joseph Manning, Jr. Although their career was short, the band has become highly influential in the power pop genre.

perplexity.description:
Bellybutton, released in 1990 by Capitol Records (originally on Charisma Records, a Capitol subsidiary), is the debut album by American rock band Jellyfish. The album is firmly rooted in power pop and rock, showcasing a blend of intricate harmonies, melodic hooks, and lush arrangements reminiscent of classic 1960s and 1970s bands like Queen and The Beatles. Its sound is characterized by bright, catchy melodies combined with a polished production style that highlights the band's musicianship and songwriting craftsmanship.

As Jellyfish's first full-length release, Bellybutton established their reputation for sophisticated pop-rock that balances accessibility with complexity. Although it did not achieve significant commercial success at the time, the album received critical praise for its ambitious and well-executed homage to classic pop and rock influences, despite some critics noting it fell short of the iconic bands it referenced. The album includes standout tracks such as "The Man I Used to Be" and "Baby's Coming Back," which exemplify the band's knack for melodic storytelling and rich vocal arrangements. Over time, Bellybutton has gained a cult following and is regarded as a significant entry in the early 1990s power pop revival.
